title: More Measures to Step Up PMD Safety
what_it_is: More Measures to Step Up PMD Safety

sections.label: PMD regulation questions to Minister
sections.summary: Questions ask the Transport Minister about reviewing PMD viability, new safety measures, certification courses, retailer compliance with UL2272, enforcement teams and online sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport in light of continuing serious casualties caused by PMDs (a) whether the Government will review the viability of PMD use in Singapore under existing regulations; (b) whether the Government intends to introduce new measures to ensure safe use of PMDs; and (c) whether the Government will consider mandatory safe-riding certification courses with disqualification rights under the law like other classes of motorists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how many physical and online retailers have agreed to stop selling e-scooters or PMDs that are non-compliant with the UL2272 standard; (b) what are the measures that LTA has taken to detect physical and online retailers that continue to advertise or sell PMDs that are non-compliant with the UL2272 standard; and (c) what are the punitive measures that LTA can adopt to act against such errant retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry will increase the number of enforcement teams to actively enforce the rules on the use of PMDs on shared footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked ask the Minister for Transport (a) what are the measures in place to deter the sale and supply of non-compliant PMDs in Singapore by online suppliers, whether local or overseas based; and (b) whether the Ministry has asked Singapore Customs to help detect and prevent non-compliant PMDs from being brought into Singapore by any supplier or individual.

sections.label: E-scooter footpath ban penalties
sections.summary: E-scooters are prohibited from all footpaths from 1 January 2020, with fines up to $2,000 and/or jail up to three months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Like France, Japan and many other countries, we have decided to prohibit the use of e-scooters from all footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: From 1 January 2020, we will carry out strict enforcement and those caught riding an e-scooter on footpaths will be liable for a fine of up to $2,000 and/or jail of up to three months.

sections.label: Cycling path network expansion
sections.summary: The dedicated cycling path network will be extended from about 440 km today to 750 km by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Overall, we will extend the network of dedicated cycling paths from about 440 km today to 750 km, latest by 2025.

sections.label: Non-UL2272 registered e-scooters
sections.summary: Of 100,000 registered e-scooters, at least 80,000 are non-UL2272 certified and cannot be used on public paths from 1 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Out of the 100,000 registered e-scooters, at least 80,000 are non-UL2272 certified and cannot be used on public paths come 1 July 2020.

sections.label: Retailer penalties and import controls
sections.summary: Twelve retailers have been caught, penalties may be raised, LTA is studying import controls, and existing applications will be rejected under a safety directive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To date, 12 retailers have been caught and dealt with by the law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We are considering raising the penalties to root out such irresponsible acts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: LTA is also studying upstream measures, including import controls, to stem the inflow of non-compliant PMDs into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As for the existing applications, we will issue a safety directive and LTA will reject them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: But it is a necessary step for pedestrians to feel safe again on public paths, while still allowing e-scooters to grow in tandem with cycling path infrastructure.

sections.label: More Active Mobility Enforcement Officers
sections.summary: The number of Active Mobility Enforcement Officers will be increased to up to 200 by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Yes, indeed, we will be increasing the number of Active Mobility Enforcement Officers (AMEOs) up to 200 by the end of this year.

sections.label: Study of AMAP recommendations
sections.summary: LTA and MOT will study some AMAP recommendations and announce later; since 1 July 2019 retailers cannot sell or advertise non-compliant PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: LTA, together with MOT, will be studying some of these recommendations by AMAP and we will make the necessary announcement later on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As to the last clarification on the sale and supply of non-compliant PMDs, I have mentioned in my reply that from 1 July 2019, retailers are already not allowed to sell or even advertise non-compliant PMDs.

sections.label: Retailers caught selling PMDs
sections.summary: All 12 retailers caught were physical retailers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Out of those 12 retailers who were caught, all of them are physical retailers.

sections.label: No PMD user licensing
sections.summary: There is no intention at this point to mandate licensing of PMD users or third-party liability insurance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As to mandatory licensing of PMD users as well as mandatory third-party liability insurance, at this point in time, we do not have the intention to do so.

sections.label: Food delivery insurance bought
sections.summary: AMAP recommended mandatory third-party liability insurance for businesses, and the three major food delivery companies bought such insurance for their PMD delivery personnel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In fact, one of the recommendations that was put forth by AMAP is to have mandatory third-party liability insurance for businesses, for example, food delivery companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I am glad to say that we have engaged the three major food delivery companies and all of them have bought third-party liability insurances for their PMD delivery personnel.

sections.label: New PMD speed limit
sections.summary: All new imported PMDs already have a speed limit of 25 km/h, the allowable speed on cycling paths and PCNs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As to the Member's supplementary question on speed limiter installation for new PMDs, in fact, currently, all the new PMDs that are imported already have a speed limit of 25 km/hour (h), which is the speed limit allowable on our cycling paths as well as our Park Connector Networks (PCNs).

sections.label: Incentive for non-compliant PMDs
sections.summary: The $100 incentive scheme is meant for PMDs that are registered but non-compliant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The incentive scheme of $100 is meant for PMDs that are registered but non-compliant.

sections.label: Town Council enforcement officers powers
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether Town Council enforcement officers could be given powers under the Active Mobility Act to enforce seamlessly, noting prohibiting PMDs on footpaths is difficult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The POZs are enforced by Town Councils and I wonder whether we could have enforcement officers appointed by the Town Councils to be also given powers under the Active Mobility Act so that these officers can enforce seamlessly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: It is a difficult decision to prohibit the use of PMDs on footpaths.

sections.label: Food delivery PMD rider numbers
sections.summary: About 7,000 food delivery riders using PMDs are engaged by three companies, likely an upper bound, and less than 30% of deliveries use PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: From our understanding, there are approximately about 7,000 food delivery riders using PMDs engaged by these three companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We think that these 7,000 riders are probably the upper bound of the number of PMD users in this trade because many of them may register under the multiple companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We also understand from the food delivery companies that less than 30% of the deliveries are actually done using PMDs.

sections.label: Alternative jobs for affected workers
sections.summary: For workers unable to convert to bicycles or motorcycles, the food delivery companies and Workforce Singapore will help look for alternative jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For those workers who are unable to convert to either bicycles or motorcycles for whatever reasons, we will be working with the food delivery companies, together with Workforce Singapore, to assist them and see how we can look for alternative jobs for them.
